question.text: This politician and general opposed the Vichy government, instead leading Free France during World War II. He later established the Fifth Republic in France.
question.answerHtml: Charles de Gaulle (accept Charles Andr´e Joseph Marie de Gaulle)
question.clue: This man answered "no" in response to the questions "must hope disappear? Is defeat final?" in his Appeal of June 18th speech.

swap.leadin: Give the following about a French religious group.
swap.text: The Edict of Saint-Germain was passed by Queen Catherine de Medici in 1572. It guaranteed private worship by this group of French Protestants.
swap.clue: These people were welcomed into Prussia via the Edict of Potsdam.

question.text: This leader of the Second French Empire was captured by the Prussians at the Battle of Sedan. He shares his name with his uncle, an earlier French emperor.
question.clue: The heavy cost of victories at Magenta and Solferino led this man to hastily conclude the Armistice of Villafranca with Austria.

swap.leadin: Name the following leaders of France.
swap.text: This Prime Minister of France, known as "the Tiger," led the French delegation at the Paris Peace Conference. His insistence on harsh German reparations made it into the Treaty of Versailles.
swap.clue: During the Dreyfus affair, this man published Emile Zola's J'Accuse letter on the front of his newspaper, L'Aurore.

question.text: This founder of the Carolingian dynasty was victorious at Tours. His grandson would go on to be the first Holy Roman Emperor.
question.clue: He served as Mayor of the Palace in Austrasia, a title he passed to his son, Pepin III after securing another victory at the Battle of Cologne.

swap.leadin: This ruler's descendants divided up his territory in the Treaty of Verdun ("ver-DUN").
swap.text: Name this Frankish ruler who was crowned Emperor by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day, 800 CE.
swap.clue: Einhard wrote a Life of this king, whose architects built an octahedral dome for the chapel of his palace at Aachen.

question.text: During the Seventh Crusade, Shajar al-Durr's forces captured this French king and held him for ransom. This king later died in Tunisia during the Eighth Crusade.
question.clue: This man's exploits were chronicled by Jean de Joinville.

swap.leadin: One group of these people, the Salians, gave their name to a system of laws banning inheritance of fiefs and kingdoms by females.
swap.text: Name these people whose lands included Austrasia and Neustria. Their later leaders included Pepin the Short and Charlemagne, who were part of their Carolingian dynasty.
swap.clue: Fantasia meant "stubbornness" or "arrogance" in a system of speech named for this word that was often used in a type of prison called a bagnio ("BAN-yo").

question.leadin: This man ordered the arrest of the Comte de Montmorency-Bouteville in an attempt to stamp out dueling among the aristocracy.
question.text: Name this man who also founded the Academie Francaise. On the Day of the Dupes, he survived an ouster attempt orchestrated by Marie de Medici.
question.answerHtml: Cardinal Richelieu [or Armand Jean du Plessis, Cardinal-Duke of Richelieu and of Fronsac]
question.clue: This successor to the Duke of Luynes implemented the reforms of the Council of Trent and was ushered into one position by Concino Concini.

swap.text: Some of Columbus's crewmen joined this French king's 1494 invasion of Italy, and may have caused the horrifically virulent epidemic that followed.
swap.clue: This man launched a campaign in which his soldiers suffered through the first recorded outbreak of syphilis in Western history.

question.leadin: An alleged form of execution used in this city called the "republican marriage" involved tying a naked man and woman together before drowning them.
question.text: What city along the Loire ("l'warr") River names an edict issued by Henry IV, which granted religious tolerance to Huguenots?
question.clue: A series of massacres took place in this city in 1793 when priests were loaded into (+) barges that were then intentionally sunk.

swap.text: The Popular Front organized the Million Franc Race to encourage competition with German automobile manufacturers, which was eventually won by a man with this last name. A man with this last name was opposed by La Libre Parole and imprisoned on Devil's Island.

question.leadin: Identify the following about medieval monastic reform movements.
question.text: This Benedictine monastery developed a large network of daughter monasteries in the 10th and 11th centuries under the abbots Odilo, Hugh the Great and Peter the Venerable. It was also home to the largest church in the world until the construction of New St. Peters.
question.clue: A head of this institution spearheaded the Truce of the Peace of God movement.

swap.text: One notable politician who had opposed the rise of the famous Napoleon III was this French socialist, who tried to implement a program of public workshops after the revolution of 1848. He supported the right of citizens to be able to work.
swap.clue: The right to work was to be guaranteed by National Workshops, workers' organizations paid by the government for public works projects, a project championed by this French socialist and historian.

question.leadin: The Duke of Brunswick was mortally wounded at this battle, where a young Carl von Clausewitz was captured.
question.text: Name this 1806 battle at which Marshal Davout ("da-VOO") routed a numerically superior Prussian army. This battle is often paired with Napoleon's victory at nearby Jena ("YAY-na").

swap.text: According to the Orkneyinga saga, the Orkneys were first subdued by the Norwegian king Harald I, whose epithet mentions this type of thing. This thing is referenced in the epithet of the first Danish king of England, who fathered Cnut the Great.
swap.answerHtml: hair [accept facial hair; accept beards; accept Harald Fairhair or Sweyn Forkbeard]
swap.clue: A king nicknamed for a lack of feature joined in the Oaths of Strasbourg and signed the Treaty of Verdun with his half-brothers Lothair and Louis the German.

question.leadin: Due to this man's paralysis, it took the executioner 15 minutes to arrange him on the guillotine.
question.text: Name this wheelchair-bound French revolutionary best remembered for drafting the Law of 22 Prairial, or the Law of Great Terror, along with Robespierre. He asked for someone to relieve him from military operations after he could not bring himself to oversee the destruction of Lyon.
question.clue: This key associate of Maximilien Robespierre and Louis Antoine de Saint-Just on the Committee of Public Safety.

swap.text: The Thermidorian Reaction marked the downfall of this faction, led by men such as Joseph-Nicolas Barbeau du Barran who sat at the highest benches in the Assembly.
swap.clue: This radical faction of the Jacobins led by Maximilien Robespierre. Their name came from their physical position in the Legislative Assembly, from which they argued with the Girondists.

question.text: The father of all commentary on Lamentations, as with the Tanach as a whole, is this 11th and 12th Century French Rabbi.

swap.text: This ex-Huguenot leader allied with Jenatsch to kick Habsburg forces out of the Valtellina valley. His brother of the same surname, the Duke of Soubise, tried to defend La Rochelle during the 1627 siege.
swap.answerHtml: Henri de Rohan [accept the Duc de Rohan or Duke of Rohan]
